humanImpact.player: CMS playback changes previously could leave a video playing or paused against the current setting. Fixed current-setting behavior without remounting.
humanImpact.keys: After reorder React could attach focus or uncontrolled input state to the wrong row/slide control. Tests demonstrate state now follows distinct content/explicit slide identities.
humanImpact.clone: Avoids unnecessary serialization work when copying relations. No production data-loss failure or measured speedup claimed for existing JSON-shaped API data.

limitations: Dynamic element children still require stable caller keys; React-generated positional keys cannot infer item identity. Existing CMS Slider and Tabs callers use stable IDs.

CMS table strings have no durable IDs. Content edits intentionally remount the affected row; identical duplicates are distinguished only by occurrence within that content, not by a nonexistent persistent identity.
structuredClone is not a JSON sanitizer; callers must preserve the existing JSON-compatible API-data contract.
Focused tests and complete serialized page-data fixtures, not a full production build or browser media-provider playback audit.
